memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Then the Lord said to Joshua, "Hold out toward Ai the javelin that is in your hand, for into your hand I will deliver the city." So Joshua held out toward the city the javelin that was in his hand. As soon as he did this, the men in the ambush rose quickly from their position and rushed forward. They entered the city and captured it and quickly set it on fire. — Josh 8:18-19 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
At God's command, Joshua stretches out his javelin toward the city, and at that signal the ambush springs into action. Ai is taken and set ablaze. This raised hand recalls another moment in Israel's history — when Moses held up his staff over the battle with Amalek, and as long as his hands were lifted, Israel prevailed (Ex 17:11). The outstretched hand was a sign that the victory belonged to God.

There is a beautiful truth pictured here. Joshua's javelin did not defeat Ai; the men did the fighting. Yet God tied the victory to Joshua's upraised hand to teach the people where their triumph truly came from. It was God who delivered the city, and the lifted hand pointed everyone's eyes to Him. God often uses simple, visible acts of obedience to remind us that He is the true source of every victory.

Notice that Joshua obeyed immediately: "So Joshua held out toward the city the javelin." No hesitation, no questioning why. When God gave the signal, Joshua responded at once, and the victory followed. Prompt obedience to God's word unleashed God's power on the field.

For us, this points to the importance of keeping our eyes fixed on God as the source of all our victories. We are prone to credit our own efforts, our cleverness, our hard work. But like the lifted javelin, everything should point back to God. And it reminds us of a greater lifting up — the Lord Jesus "lifted up" on the cross, through whom God won the decisive victory over sin and death for us (John 12:32). Our victory, too, was won by outstretched hands.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. When you succeed, do your "eyes" point back to God, or to yourself?
2. Do you obey God's signals promptly, as Joshua did, or hesitate?
3. How does Christ "lifted up" on the cross assure you the greatest victory is already won?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, keep my eyes fixed on You as the source of every victory. Give me prompt obedience, and thank You for the triumph won through Christ lifted up for me. Amen.
